title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class rho with a cyclotomic-squaring branch, trails restarted at distinguished points and exponents recovered by replay

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT in the van Oorschot-Wiener trail form: every trail runs from a fresh uniform start g^alpha0 z^beta0 to its first distinguished point, where (F, alpha0, beta0) is appended to the report log and the walk begins a new trail; 2^20 walks round-robin on one processor, R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, a Granger-Scott cyclotomic-squaring branch taken iff T mod 64 < 37 with branch, multiplier and distinguished-point bits read from the stored class invariant T=Re(c_0), deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes, hard caps on reports, stuck-walk restarts and matcher pairs, no per-step exponent bookkeeping (the exponents of a matched pair are recovered by replaying its two trails), and a pre-debit work meter whose walk-phase budget leaves the setup bound and a reserved stopping allowance; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds, in the ideal model, with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.111 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000) on every run, including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts and fresh starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, matching (sort, duplicate removal, replays and pair checks), output and verification. A multiply step is charged 16,578 instructions (the 14,402-instruction table-multiply kernel, 2,014 of key work and 162 of every-step bookkeeping) and a squaring step 6,939 (the 6,777-instruction squaring kernel and 162), 0.55027265625 units per step on average; the nominal ledger is below 2^125.0856 and 2^125.111 is the least thousandth that also covers a 2-percentage-point drop of the squaring fraction. Peak memory is below 2^63 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for rho walks adjusted for the branch mix (effective class count N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)), with model success 0.4005, at least 0.3904 after the 0.01 allowed for heuristic H1+ (no percentage-point drift of the walk statistics, and the caps) and the small loss terms of proof.md section 4; it is supported by toy-field experiments of this trail discipline and by the production branch rule run in the real BLS12-381 GT. No production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: BLS12-381 GT identities (Re(c_0) across the 12 conjugates, Frobenius formula, 4-multiplication key, distinctness, canonical representative, Granger-Scott squaring counts, r-1 factorisation). Part C: the production branch rule (T mod 64, low table-index bits) on real GT for 2,000 steps per rule vs explicit Frobenius. Part B: the complete algorithm (trails restarted at distinguished points, cycle escapes, a report log of (F, alpha0, beta0) records, heapsort matcher, replay of both trails of every matched pair with a check that the replay ends at the recorded class, pair budget, collision solving) in a toy field vs the branch-adjusted random-mapping law. Part E: pair-collision law. Part D: read measure/, assert the blst marginals and kernel prices, recompute the ledger, caps, cap inequality, matcher worst case, stopping allowance and non-walk sum. Part S: the bounded sampler. flags_check.py: the multiword compares/increments under AArch64 NZCV. Toy scale only; no production costs.
